title: Chain Letter
tagline: Trace the letters. Find the words. Beat the dictionary.
teaser: Sixteen letter cubes, three minutes, and a dictionary that knows every word hiding in them. Drag across neighbouring letters to chain words together, light up the grid, and see how much of the board you can claim. A 1988 word hunt from a Vancouver computer lab, reborn.

manPage.synopsis: Chain Letter — trace words through touching letter cubes, then see every word the board held and your share of it.
manPage.description: Barry Brachman's word hunt from the University of British Columbia, written in 1988 for a Sun 3 and an Atari 1040ST, reborn with cubes you can almost pick up. You play against the dictionary: when the bell rings, the board lights up with every word it held and your share of them becomes your board-reading level. The 1988 rule switches return as the Echo and Mirror cards, alongside a Daily Grid, a Duel with an AI word-hunter, and a word book for rare finds.

howToPlay: Drag across touching cubes, diagonals included, to spell a word; or type it and press Enter.
Points grow with length, and quick finds build a chain up to ×3.
When time is up you see every word the board held; your share of them is the number to beat.
